recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Future changes to GET or POST search conformance should be handled by a new FHIR-I decision, not by restoring FHIR-18551's superseded wording to the Search page.
issue_request: FHIR-18551 asked to add a Search-page conformance requirement for GET and POST search. After reopening, its final Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution was that a server supporting search SHALL support POST-based search and SHOULD support GET-based search, and implementation guides may make GET required where needed.
initial_application: No source-changing commit explicitly naming FHIR-18551 was found. The old proposal to add SHALL-both wording was revised before final disposition; later R5 search-page work added GET/POST examples and self-link guidance, and FHIR-39137 moved protocol conformance material from source/search.html to active source/http.html.
additional_context: FHIR-18551 is part of the FHIR-30577/FHIR-31912/FHIR-31943/FHIR-31944 search-method family. Later final issue FHIR-31943 superseded the literal POST-SHALL/GET-SHOULD wording with a GET/POST plus 405 model; FHIR-31944 clarified POST parameter and self-link behavior; FHIR-38994 and FHIR-39137 aligned and moved the HTTP/Search guidance. Zulip editor follow-up explicitly says FHIR-31943 and FHIR-31944 supersede FHIR-18551 and FHIR-31912.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Search page directs protocol details to the HTTP Search section and contains GET/POST-aware examples and self-link guidance, while the active HTTP page carries the current GET/POST support, 405 response, POST-parameter, and method-choice wording. Restoring FHIR-18551's literal sentence would duplicate text and conflict with later final decisions.
